svg.title: One multilingual model, many transfer paths
svg.desc: A multilingual model shares a vocabulary and Transformer weights across languages. Fine-tuning on English and testing on Hindi is zero-shot cross-lingual transfer. Shared subwords, structure, and representation geometry help; data imbalance and fixed capacity make transfer uneven, so sampling with n_i^alpha can up-weight smaller languages.

g.text: One multilingual model, many transfer paths
Shared tokens and weights help languages transfer—but data and capacity stay uneven.
SHARE ONE VOCABULARY AND ONE MODEL
Objective can stay monolingual; transfer is a side effect.
WHY TRANSFER WORKS—and WHY IT CAN BE UNEVEN
Sampling by nᵢ^α (α < 1) gives low-resource languages more weight than raw corpus size.
